headline: Google Assistant begins shutdown Sept 4, 2026, replaced by Gemini on phones & watches
summary: Google has confirmed that its Assistant will start phasing out on September 4, 2026, with Gemini taking over on Android phones, Wear OS, and earbuds. This transition was initially expected earlier but was delayed.
details: Google Assistant will officially begin its shutdown on September 4, 2026, as confirmed by emails sent to users. This process marks the transition of the mobile assistant experience from Assistant to Gemini, taking several weeks to complete.

The initial phase-out will impact Android phones, Wear OS watches, and Assistant-compatible earbuds and headphones, where Gemini will become the default assistant. Access on Android Auto will also be affected.

However, not all devices are included in this shutdown. Google Assistant will continue to be available on cars with Google built-in, smart displays, speakers, and other Assistant-compatible devices even after the September 4 deadline.

Once the transition is complete, invoking the assistant on affected Android phones by saying "Hey Google" or long-pressing the power button will trigger Gemini. Users still relying on Assistant have approximately 30 days to make the switch.

Google had previously announced the Assistant's demise before the end of 2025, then pushed the deadline to March 2026, and now to September 2026. This delay has allowed Gemini to receive significant improvements throughout the year.

While Gemini initially had some rough edges, it has since evolved to surpass its predecessor in many aspects. Its superior natural language understanding and conversational abilities make it a more capable assistant for everyday tasks.

headline_marked: [[OpenCode is the open-source coding agent]] supporting 75+ LLMs, surpassing Claude Code
headline: OpenCode is the open-source coding agent supporting 75+ LLMs, surpassing Claude Code
summary: This Go-built terminal agent offers unparalleled model flexibility, allowing developers to use any LLM from local models to major providers, without subscriptions or vendor lock-in.
details: OpenCode is an open-source AI coding agent built in Go, designed to run in the terminal, desktop, and IDE. It operates on a "bring the model, OpenCode brings the agent" thesis, supporting over 75 LLM providers. It doesn't store code, charge subscriptions, and serves over 7.5 million developers monthly.

Developed by the SST team, OpenCode has surpassed Claude Code in GitHub stars (160K+ vs 122K+), becoming the most starred open-source coding agent. Its client/server architecture drives a terminal TUI, a desktop app, and IDE extensions for VS Code and Cursor.

The agent features a polished TUI with 'Build' and 'Plan' modes. Build mode executes tasks directly, while Plan mode allows the agent to analyze the codebase and propose an approach before any file modification, offering a clear separation of intent and execution.

Unlike Claude Code, which is tuned for Anthropic's models, OpenCode connects to 75+ providers via Models.dev, including Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, and local runtimes like Ollama. Users can switch models mid-session, a feature not available in Claude Code.

OpenCode offers flexible pricing: "Bring your own key" for direct provider rates, "OpenCode Zen" as a hosted gateway, and "OpenCode Go" at $10/month for access to capable open models. This contrasts with Claude Code's higher subscription tiers.

A key event in January 2026 saw Anthropic block third-party apps like OpenCode from authenticating users via Claude.ai accounts. While Claude models are still usable with an Anthropic API key, this reinforced OpenCode's philosophical stance on open vs. managed products.

OpenCode is praised for its user experience, with its TUI being a favorite for its smooth updates and independent scrolling sections. It also provides standalone Tauri desktop apps for macOS, Windows, and Linux, a feature absent in Claude Code.

However, Claude Code offers a wider toolset, including Agent View for fleet management, /goal for autonomous runs, and instant rewind. OpenCode counters with background subagents and sessions that persist across terminal restarts.
